description: Colorado individual income tax rate schedule, applied to Colorado taxable income. A flat rate is a schedule with one bracket.
keyed_by: first day of the income tax year (calendar-year filers assumed)

values.conflict_note: The ingested statute text states 4.40% 'Except as otherwise provided in section 39-22-627' (temporary rate adjustment to refund excess state revenues). The Department of Revenue publishes 4.25% for 2024, so the agency value is used. The 39-22-627 text on the same mirror describes only a 4.63% to 4.50% reduction and cannot produce 4.25%, so the mirror snapshot predates the provision that set this rate. That provision has not been ingested.

values.caveat: The Department of Revenue's rate table stopped at 2025 when read on 2026-11-11. The statutory 4.40% applies unless a temporary reduction under section 39-22-627 is made for 2026; none was confirmed or ruled out.

sources.publisher: Colorado Legislative Council Staff (file stamped 'CDOS Received: January 9, 2026', initiative 2025-2026 #195, final text)
sources.quote: WITH RESPECT TO TAXABLE YEARS COMMENCING ON OR AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, A GRADUATED TAX IS IMPOSED ON FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME

sources.publisher: Colorado Legislative Council Staff, 2026 Blue Book, Amendment 87
sources.quote: income tax brackets are not adjusted for inflation

sources.summary: Amendment 87 (2026): 3.7% to $25,000; 4.2% to $100,000; 4.4% to $500,000; 7.4% to $750,000; 7.9% to $1 million; 8.4% above; tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2027.

values.caveat: Election result was unofficial and uncertified as of 2026-11-11; no certification was found. The brackets are derived from the measure's proposed (1.8)(a), ingested in text/co-2026-amendment-87.xml. The text sets one schedule for every individual, estate and trust, with no filing-status thresholds, and the Blue Book says the brackets are not adjusted for inflation. The base is federal taxable income as modified by 39-22-104 (3) and (4). Not modelled: proposed (1.8)(b), which taxes certain gain on the sale of a principal residence at 4.40% (the engine refuses a filer who reports such gain), and any temporary rate change under section 39-22-627, to which (1.8)(a) is expressly subject.
